title: Yara and the Orbit
premise: Ansel Ishikawa, a clone grown from the murdered founder Yara Okonkwo's tissue, tends the orbital beacon above colony Meridian-9 while the original's unsolved killing festers in his inherited memories. When the colony's children begin dreaming a shared nightmare of a massacre that official records insist never happened, Ansel realizes his fragmented genetic memory holds the truth. As the jump window — the only ship departure for eleven years — closes, Ansel and a found family of dreamers race to recover erased evidence hidden inside the beacon itself. He proves the massacre occurred, exposes the administrator dynasty that ordered it, and chooses to stay behind as the new beacon's living archive rather than flee.
about_author: L. M. Okonkwo is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent six years at a remote listening station before turning to fiction. Their work explores what survives of us when institutions decide what is worth remembering.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. He performs routine maintenance on the ancient orbital beacon, haunted by flashes of Yara's final day that he cannot place. The colony below ignores him; supply manifests show no record of the beacon ever being commissioned. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness and the first crack of doubt about his own purpose.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Night
chapters.summary: Dual POV: schoolteacher Imka Voss notices thirty children describing an identical dream of fire in a wheat field and a door marked with seven lines. She files a report that vanishes into Administrator Sefu Hale's office. Emotional beat: creeping unease as ordinary life shows its first hairline fracture.

chapters.title: Inherited Hands
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A medical scan reveals his cloned brain carries engram patterns no cloning license permits — deliberate memory transfer. He recalls, unbidden, Yara screaming a name: 'Hale.' Emotional beat: horror at discovering he was made to remember something someone wanted buried.

chapters.title: The Dreamer Who Woke Up
chapters.summary: Child POV: ten-year-old Bex, the strongest dreamer, describes the massacre's final image — people sealed in the hydroponics vault. Imka brings Bex to Ansel, believing the beacon's signal causes the dreams. Emotional beat: tentative connection between two outsiders guarding the same secret from opposite ends.

chapters.title: Records of Nothing
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. He requests colonial archives and finds Year One scrubbed: population logs jump from 4,000 to 3,100 with no explanation, deaths listed as 'relocation.' Sefu Hale summons him for a polite, chilling conversation. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing erasure was professional, thorough work.

chapters.title: Seven Lines on a Door
chapters.summary: Imka's POV. She deciphers the children's recurring symbol as a tally carved inside the hydroponics vault door — but the vault was decommissioned and welded shut decades ago. Hale places her on administrative leave. Emotional beat: defiance hardening into resolve at personal cost.

chapters.title: What the Clone Remembers
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Under Bex's dreaming guidance, Ansel unlocks a full memory: Yara discovering that First Administrator Odile Hale ordered dissenters gassed in the vault, then rewriting history. Yara hid proof in the beacon before being killed. Emotional beat: grief arriving like weather — Yara's death becomes his own mourning.

chapters.title: The Found Family
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation. Ansel, Imka, Bex, and disgraced archivist Tomas Reyes form a fragile conspiracy in the beacon's maintenance bay. Each confesses why they can't let it go. Emotional beat: warmth kindling — for the first time, Ansel belongs to something chosen, not manufactured.

chapters.title: Signal in the Static
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The team discovers the beacon broadcasts a low-band carrier wave — Yara's encrypted data packet, looping for forty years, which seeded the children's dreams through neural implant firmware updates. Emotional beat: awe that the dead woman has been speaking all along.

chapters.title: Hale Closes In
chapters.summary: Sefu Hale's POV, first time. He knows what the beacon carries; his family has maintained the lie for three generations. He orders the beacon decommissioned and schedules its demolition — timed just before the jump window opens. Emotional beat: cold dread; the antagonist moves with institutional inevitability.

chapters.title: Sabotage and Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A demolition crew arrives early; Ansel stalls them with forged maintenance orders while Bex smuggles out the decryption core. Imka is detained. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into competence — Ansel stops apologizing for existing.

chapters.title: The Vault Below
chapters.summary: Bex's POV. Guided by the dream's geography, Bex leads Tomas through disused tunnels to the sealed hydroponics vault. They find the tally marks — real, physical, 900 scratches — and bone fragments the cleanup missed. Emotional beat: childhood innocence colliding with atrocity, handled with terrible gentleness.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Teacher
chapters.summary: Imka's POV. Sefu interrogates her, offering reinstatement in exchange for the children's names. She refuses, and he reveals the family doctrine: 'Memory is a debt we chose not to pay.' Emotional beat: moral clarity under pressure; she understands exactly what she'll lose.

chapters.title: Decryption
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The team cracks Yara's packet: video testimony, shipping manifests for the gas, and Odile Hale's own voice authorizing the operation. But broadcasting it requires the beacon's main array — scheduled for demolition in nine days, when the jump window opens. Emotional beat: triumph immediately shadowed by the ticking clock.

chapters.title: The Colony Must Choose
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Leaked fragments spread through the colony's implant network; adults begin dreaming too. Public opinion splits — some demand truth, others beg to keep the comfortable lie before boarding the jump ship. Emotional beat: a community tearing along the seam between inheritance and denial.

chapters.title: Betrayal
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas, offered amnesty and a seat on the jump ship, hands Hale the decryption core's location. He justifies it as protecting the children from reprisal. Emotional beat: heartbreak — found family wounded not by enemies but by fear inside their own circle.

chapters.title: Siege of the Beacon
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Hale's security storms the beacon. Ansel seals himself in the array control room, buying hours by venting atmosphere section by section. Bex reaches him through the dream-link one last time: 'She said you'd know how to finish it.' Emotional beat: isolation transfigured into communion with the dead.

chapters.title: Yara's Last Day
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, interlude. Forty years earlier: her final twenty-four hours — hiding the data, carving nothing, dying at Hale's order while the beacon carried her testimony skyward. Emotional beat: the murder case finally witnessed whole; the reader sees everything Ansel inherited.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, climax. With demolition charges armed and security breaching the door, Ansel overrides the array and transmits Yara's full testimony across every colony channel and the jump ship's receivers. The children's dream plays publicly as corroborating evidence. Emotional beat: catharsis — the silenced voice fills the entire sky.

chapters.title: The Reckoning
chapters.summary: Imka's POV. Sefu Hale, confronted by colonists and crew, tries to board the jump ship and is refused passage by the captain citing Yara's broadcast. Colonial charter law revives: the Hales' authority dissolves. Tomas, broken, surrenders the core and asks for no forgiveness. Emotional beat: justice without satisfaction — accountability, not vengeance.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The ship departs with half the colony aboard; those remaining vote to exhume the vault and build a memorial. Imka asks Ansel to come if another window ever opens. He watches the drive-flare fade beside Bex and the children. Emotional beat: bittersweet release — leaving is possible now, which makes staying a choice.

chapters.title: Living Archive
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, coda. One year later: the beacon rebuilt as a memorial transmitter, carrying both Yara's testimony and the colonists' own recorded memories. Ansel adds his first entry — his own name, freely chosen. Emotional beat: peace; inheritance transformed from burden into gift, and a clone into a person.
